spans.s:
Raghaṭ occurs once in the plural in the Atharvaveda,^1 where
the Paippalāda recension reads vaghaṭah. Roth^2 once con-
[]
jectured raghavaḥ, ‘swift,’ as the correct reading. Bloomfield,^3
who in his translation explains the word as ‘falcons,’ in his
notes inclines to think Roth's conjecture likely. Ludwig^4
suggests ‘bees’ as the meaning. Possibly some kind of bird
may be intended.^5
1) viii. 7, 24.
2) St. Petersburg Dictionary, s.v., 1a.
3) Hymns of the Atharvaveda, 580.
4) Translation of the Rigveda, 3, 504.
5) Böhtlingk, Dictionary, s.v. Cf.
Whitney, Translation of the Atharva-
veda, 501.
